Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Order form caps — proposed redistribution

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We reviewed Exhibit B and have one substantive ask before we can circulate to our legal: can Redwood accommodate a reallocation of the unused cap from SKU 'NLP-Base' into SKU 'NLP-Scale' within the same term rather than issuing a cash credit?

Our rationale: we have a bursty forecast shift that would leave base capacity underutilized but will increase consumption on the scaled SKU. We prefer a capacity reallocation because it simplifies our monthly true-ups and preserves unit pricing.

Attached: Acme_ExhibitB_Redline_v1.pdf with inline comments (see pg. 3–5). Specific requests:
- Shift up to 25% of unused Base commit to Scale SKU during Q3–Q4 2026 (one-time transfer)
- If transfer unused, apply a surcharge offset smoothing clause so there is no invoice volatility in the following two months

Can you confirm whether this is commercially acceptable and, if so, provide a tracked-changes order form reflecting the change? If not, please propose an alternate (one-time credit, refund, or carryover) and outline the invoicing mechanics.

Thanks,
Sara

Naomi / team / Sara — thanks for the context and the redline. Quick legal read: conceptually OK, but we need bright-line definitions and a reconciliation timeline. Proposed legal points to preserve: 

1) Definition of "Unused Commit": unconsumed committed units as of the last day of the prior billing month, verified by Redwood usage reports.
2) Transfer Window: transfer must be executed within a 30-day election window following written notice; transferred units must be consumed within the original contract term unless otherwise agreed.
3) Surcharge Offset Smoothing: instead of altering invoice lines retroactively, Redwood will apply an amortized credit across the next two billing cycles to offset any surcharge differential caused by the transfer.
4) Audit Right: Acme may request a one-time audit of usage for the affected months; Redwood will provide CSV usage export and logs.

Open question for commercial: do we allow partial transfers that split a unit between SKUs (i.e., fractional units)? I recommend whole-unit transfers to keep invoicing consistent.

I'll mark these in Exhibit B and send a tracked-changes version once Ben confirms the commercial approach.

—Marissa

Hi all — commercial approach and quick estimate below. We recommend two options for Acme:

Option A (preferred): One-time internal transfer of up to 25% of unused Base commit to Scale SKU during the transfer window. Units transfer at the existing contracted unit price for Scale SKU. To smooth invoice volatility, Redwood will apply an amortized offset credit over the next two billing cycles equal to the net surcharge delta.

Option B: One-time credit equal to the monetary value of the transferred units (calculated at Base unit price), applied against future invoices until exhausted.

Estimated impact (example):
- Unused Base units to transfer: 10,000 tokens equivalent
- Unit price Base: $0.0009 / token; Scale price: $0.0014 / token
- Net surcharge delta (if transferred to Scale): (0.0014 - 0.0009) * 10,000 = $5.00 (example values for illustration)
- Amortized offset: $2.50 applied to each of the next two invoices

Notes:
- Fractional units: we recommend whole-unit transfers only (clean invoicing).
- Accounting: transfers will be reflected on the monthly invoice as an Annex line item with supporting usage export.

I've attached a lightweight pricing-impact-estimate.xlsx with the math and a draft annex language snippet. If Acme prefers Option B, we'll need to confirm tax treatment in each jurisdiction.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Ben
